story.see: Across the Ararat Valley, towns, ponds and fields share the radar image. Some dry slopes return a weak echo and can look like water. We use elevation to screen dark patches on steep or high ground. Individual ponds and fields remain difficult to track consistently.
story.physics: A preview pixel is roughly 180 metres wide. After the terrain screen, the open-water rule mapped about 0.5 to 3.8 square kilometres on different passes in our test box. Much of that area remains uncertain, and the comparison with historical water shows that many small water bodies are missed.
story.lband: From Masis toward Vedi, the radar echo can change with wet soil, crops and surface roughness. An unusual cross-polarized echo on 6 October adds uncertainty. Sharper calibrated images and dated ground observations would help us test specific irrigation or harvest changes.
story.people: Farms and fish ponds in the valley use artesian groundwater. The US Geological Survey found that the area with flowing wells fell from 619 to 291 square kilometres between 1984 and 2016. The ponds give us a surface feature to watch. Well readings tell us about groundwater.
